note: Wiki pages and onboarding lessons. Every rule here must match Balance.json and the simulation (Simulator.cs, Layout.cs). Live numbers (costs, kW, sizes) are added by code from Balance.json. Lessons marked required must be seen once before the levels that list them in 'needs'; after that they can be skipped or replayed from the Wiki.

steps.speaker: teacher
steps.text: A civilization needs more than buildings. It needs people, resources, science and a plan.
steps.more: Let's turn your drawing into a plan a real crew could live in.

steps.speaker: teacher
steps.text: Great drawing! Each building on it has a job.

cards.title: Habitat
cards.text: Home for the crew. Uses power.

cards.title: Greenhouse
cards.text: Grows food. Needs soil, water, power.

steps.more: A real base also needs Air Support, a Battery, a Radio Dish and a Rover Garage. You will meet them later.

steps.speaker: teacher
steps.text: A base runs on resources. You will see them at the top of the screen.

cards.title: Water
cards.text: To drink and to grow plants.

steps.more: Hover over or tap any number in the top bar to see what it means.

steps.speaker: teacher
steps.text: Buildings make, store and use resources.
steps.more: Air Support uses power to make air. The Greenhouse uses power and water to make food. If power out is bigger than power in, the Battery drains.

steps.speaker: teacher
steps.text: Buildings help each other when they are close.

cards.title: Battery
cards.text: Near Solar Arrays: no wasted power.

cards.title: Air Support
cards.text: Next to the Habitat: more air.

cards.title: Greenhouse
cards.text: Next to Air Support: saves power.

cards.title: Rover Garage
cards.text: Near soil and water: quick trips.

steps.more: When you pick a building, green glowing tiles show good spots. They are only tips: you may build on any allowed tile.

steps.speaker: teacher
steps.text: Plan first, then build. Four rules to start:
steps.more: Stuck? Press Wiki at the bottom left. It explains every building, resource and event.

steps.speaker: narrator
steps.text: Years later, at the space agency. Today you meet the crew you will lead.

steps.speaker: engineer
steps.text: Hi, Commander! I'm Priya, the engineer. I love a careful plan.

steps.speaker: engineer
steps.text: My job is power. Your job: keep power in bigger than power out.

replies.answer: The base switches off what can wait. Air Support stays on longest.
Air Support makes our air. Without power, the air runs down.

steps.more: When power runs short, things switch off in this order: Radio Dish and Rover Garage, then Greenhouse, then Shelter.

steps.speaker: botanist
steps.text: I'm Mateo, the botanist. Plants make me happy, and they feed us!

steps.speaker: botanist
steps.text: My Greenhouse needs soil, water and power. Yuki's rover brings the soil and water.

replies.text: Where should the Rover Garage go?
replies.answer: Near brown soil dots and blue water dots. Short trips are faster.

steps.more: The rover fetches soil first. When there is enough for the Greenhouse, it fetches water.

steps.speaker: geologist
steps.text: I'm Yuki, the geologist. I explore outside, study rocks and search for minerals and ice.

steps.speaker: geologist
steps.text: When I'm far away, call me on the Radio Dish. Without power, I can't hear you.

steps.speaker: geologist
steps.text: Sometimes the Sun throws out fast particles: a solar storm. Mission control warns us first.

replies.answer: No. The Sun still shines. Solar Arrays keep working.
Warnings in the Information panel, and my name in the crew list.

steps.more: The particles arrive about 12 hours after the warning. Crew outside, or without a powered Shelter, lose crew safety.

steps.speaker: you
steps.text: My crew counts on me: power for Priya, soil and water for Mateo, a radio link for Yuki.

wiki.title: How to play
wiki.summary: Six steps to a working base.

rows.text: 1. Place the Habitat first. All other buildings must be within 6 tiles of it.
2. Put Air Support next to the Habitat (1 tile or less). It makes air.
3. Build Solar Arrays on bright ground. Power in must beat power out.
4. Put a Battery within 2 tiles of your Solar Arrays to save spare power.
5. A Rover Garage near soil and water fetches soil for the Greenhouse.
6. Pause any time to think. When time runs out, your base is inspected. That is not a failure.

wiki.title: Reading the screen
wiki.summary: Where everything is.

rows.text: Top bar: your resources. Hover over or tap a number to learn more.
Top right: the time, Pause, the speed button (1×, 2×, 4×) and the inspection countdown.
Left: your crew. Click a crew member to talk. The Wiki button is below them.
Right, top: Information. Warnings and messages for the commander.
Right, bottom: Objectives. Each one gets a tick when it is done.
Bottom: Buildings. Pick one, then click the map.

wiki.title: Controls
wiki.summary: Mouse first. Touch works too.

rows.text: Click a building card, then click the map. Right-click or press Cancel to stop.
Click a building on the map to see what it needs. Some can be turned off.
Space: pause or resume. H: open this Wiki. Esc: menu.

wiki.title: Habitat
wiki.summary: Home for the crew. Build it first.
wiki.best: Pick a place with bright ground nearby. Every other building must be within 6 tiles of it.

rows.text: The crew lives here. Your base grows around it.
Uses power all the time. If it has no power for 10 hours, the mission stops.
Put Air Support within 1 tile of it for full air.

wiki.title: Solar Array
wiki.summary: Turns sunlight into power.
wiki.best: Bright ground, within 2 tiles of a Battery. Far from a Battery, a long cable wastes 30% of its power.

rows.text: Makes up to 3 kW in full sun. Darker ground makes less.
Spare power goes into the Battery.
Shadows and dust storms lower its power. A solar storm does not.

wiki.title: Battery
wiki.summary: Saves spare power for later.
wiki.best: Within 2 tiles of your Solar Arrays: short cables waste no power.

rows.text: Charges when power in beats power out. Gives power back when it runs short.
It can charge or give at most 5 kW at a time.
You start with one. A second one unlocks after your first long shadow or dust storm.

wiki.title: Air Support
wiki.summary: Makes air for the crew to breathe.
wiki.best: Next to the Habitat (1 tile or less). A Greenhouse right next to it saves 1 kW.

rows.text: Within 1 tile of the Habitat, it adds 2 hours of air every hour. Farther away, a long air pipe halves that.
Needs power. Without power, the air goes down 1 hour every hour.
If the air runs out, the mission stops. Never let it lose power.

wiki.title: Radio Dish
wiki.summary: Lets you talk to your crew and Earth.

rows.text: You need it to call Yuki back to base in a solar storm.
Needs power. It is the first thing switched off when power runs short.

wiki.title: Greenhouse
wiki.summary: Grows food. Needs soil, power and water.
wiki.best: Right next to Air Support (1 tile): the plants help clean the air, so Air Support uses 1 kW less.

rows.text: Costs 6 bags of soil. The rover brings soil.
Grows half a meal every hour and adds a little air.
Uses water, but recycles most of it. With no water, it stops growing.
Your first harvest brings 30 supplies. If the Shelter is locked, it unlocks it.

wiki.title: Shelter
wiki.summary: Protects the crew from solar particles.
wiki.best: Within 2 tiles of the Habitat. Farther away, it only half protects the crew.

rows.text: When it is switched on and powered, the crew inside is safe from storm particles.
It starts switched off. Turn it on when a storm warning comes.
Unlocks after your first harvest.

wiki.title: Rover Garage
wiki.summary: Its rover fetches soil, then water.
wiki.best: Within 2 tiles of soil and 3 tiles of water. Short trips are faster. Farther than 8 tiles, the rover cannot go.

rows.text: First it brings soil, 2 bags a trip, until you have enough for the Greenhouse.
Then it brings water, 1.5 L a trip.
Needs power. It switches off early when power runs short.

wiki.title: Power
wiki.summary: Power in from Solar Arrays, minus power out to buildings.

rows.text: Made by Solar Arrays. Measured in kW.
Spare power charges the Battery.
When power runs short, the base switches off: Radio Dish and Rover Garage, then Greenhouse, then Shelter. Habitat and Air Support stay on longest.

wiki.title: Battery
wiki.summary: Power saved for later, in kWh.

rows.text: Each Battery holds 12 kWh.
It fills when you have spare power and empties when you do not.

wiki.title: Air
wiki.summary: Hours of air (oxygen) left for the crew.

rows.text: Air Support makes it. The most you can store is 36 hours.
A working Greenhouse adds a little air too.
Without powered Air Support, air drops 1 hour every hour. At 0, the mission stops.

wiki.title: Water
wiki.summary: Litres of water for drinking and plants.

rows.text: The crew drinks a little every hour.
The Greenhouse uses some, but recycles most.
The rover brings more: ice on the Moon, wet clay on Mars. At 0, the mission stops.

wiki.title: Food
wiki.summary: Meals left for the crew.

rows.text: Three crew eat 3 meals a day each: 9 a day.
The Greenhouse grows more. At 0, the mission stops.

wiki.title: Soil
wiki.summary: Bags of soil for the Greenhouse.

rows.text: The rover brings soil from brown tiles. You can keep up to 12 bags.
The Greenhouse needs 6 bags to build.

wiki.title: Crew safety
wiki.summary: How safe the crew is from solar particles.

rows.text: Drops in a solar storm if someone is outside, or the Shelter is off or has no power.
Comes back slowly when everyone is safe. Below 50% for 2 hours, the mission stops.

wiki.title: Supplies
wiki.summary: Building materials. Every building costs supplies.

rows.text: Supply landers bring more. Your first harvest brings 30.
Removing a building gives its supplies back. Fixing a broken Solar Array costs 5.

wiki.title: Buildings that help each other
wiki.summary: Where you build changes how well it works.

rows.text: Solar Array within 2 tiles of a Battery: no power lost in the cable.
Air Support within 1 tile of the Habitat: full air. Farther: half.
Greenhouse next to Air Support: Air Support uses 1 kW less.
Shelter within 2 tiles of the Habitat: full protection.
Rover Garage near soil and water: faster trips.
Good links also raise the Layout part of your grade.

wiki.title: What makes what
wiki.summary: Each building turns some resources into others.

rows.text: Sunlight makes power. Power runs every other building.
Air Support: power makes air.
Rover Garage: power makes soil trips, then water trips.
Greenhouse: soil (to build), power and water make food and a little air.
Radio Dish: power lets you call the crew.
Shelter: power keeps the crew safe in a storm.

wiki.title: Priya, Engineer
wiki.summary: Careful planner. Looks after power.

rows.text: Looks after Solar Arrays and the Battery.
Needs from you: power in bigger than power out. Switch off what can wait.

wiki.title: Mateo, Botanist
wiki.summary: Cheerful plant lover. Grows the food.

rows.text: Runs the Greenhouse.
Needs from you: soil and water from the rover, and power for the Greenhouse.

wiki.title: Yuki, Geologist
wiki.summary: Curious explorer. Drives the rover and studies rocks.

rows.text: Explores outside and searches for minerals and ice.
Needs from you: a powered Radio Dish, so you can call her in.
In a solar storm she is outside. Call her in early.

wiki.title: Solar storm
wiki.summary: Fast particles from the Sun. Mission control warns you first.

rows.text: The warning comes about 12 hours before the particles arrive.
1. Call Yuki in. The Radio Dish needs power.
2. Switch on the Shelter and keep it powered.
3. Short on power? Rest the Greenhouse.
The Sun still shines. Solar Arrays keep working.
If you do not call her, Yuki heads back 1 hour after the particles arrive, and crew safety drops.

wiki.title: Long shadow and dust storm
wiki.summary: Less sun for a while. Solar Arrays make less power.

rows.text: A warning comes 8 hours before. Charge the Battery.
Rest the Greenhouse if power runs short.
Getting through the first one unlocks a second Battery.

wiki.title: Other events
wiki.summary: Landers, harvests, sunrise and space rocks.

rows.text: Supply lander: brings more supplies.
First harvest: 30 supplies.
Space rock: breaks a Solar Array. Fix it for 5 supplies.
Sunrise: sunlight creeps over the ridge and solar power climbs.

wiki.title: Inspection and grades
wiki.summary: When time runs out, mission control grades your base.

rows.text: The countdown at the top right shows when the inspection comes.
Grades: S 81+, A 61+, B 31+, C 0+. Running out of time is never a failure.
Points come from goals, layout, crew safety, reserves and steady power.

wiki.title: Reading the map
wiki.summary: Bright ground, soil, water and rocks.

rows.text: Brighter ground gets more sun, so Solar Arrays make more power there.
Brown dots: soft soil for the rover.
Blue dots: ice on the Moon. Teal dots: wet clay on Mars.
Dark rocks and craters: you cannot build there.
While placing, the dark area is outside your base. You cannot build there.
Green glow: a suggested spot. It is a tip, not a rule.

wiki.title: Teacher's Lesson
wiki.summary: Buildings, resources and planning.

rows.text: Solar Arrays make power. A Battery stores it. Buildings use it.
Resources: power, air, water, food, soil and supplies.
Close buildings help each other.
Habitat first, bright ground for Solar Arrays, power in beats power out, air before plants.

wiki.title: Meet the Crew
wiki.summary: Priya, Mateo and Yuki.

rows.text: Priya needs steady power.
Mateo needs soil and water from the rover.
Yuki needs a powered Radio Dish. Call her in when a storm warning comes.
